reference.title: Barbell Quarter Squat
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it through the short dip, breathe out as you stand.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, a short pause, about 1 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: the short range lets you handle more than your full-squat weight, so build up in small steps and leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when every rep reaches the same depth with a flat back.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed together. Step back from the rack, feet about hip to shoulder width, toes turned out a little.
Brace, then bend the hips and knees together and sink only about a quarter of the way down: knees about 60 degrees, chest up.
Stop at the same depth every rep; no bounce.
Drive the floor away and stand tall, hips and knees straightening together. Breathe out at the top.
Stand tall, re-brace before the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Depth creeping shallower as the set goes on
mistakes.fix: Pick a depth (a box or a pin just under you helps) and touch the same point every rep.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning forward so the hips do all the work
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and the bar over mid-foot; bend the knees as much as the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Locking the knees hard at the top
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with the knees straight but not snapped back.

mistakes.mistake: Loading far beyond what the back can hold
mistakes.fix: Add weight in small steps; the trunk has to support the bar however short the range.

kinematics.norm: About hip to shoulder width, toes out about 10-30 degrees (Lorenzetti 2018)
A quarter squat stops at about 40-70 degrees of knee flexion; a full squat goes past 110 (clinical opinion; Straub 2024)
Small forward lean in a shallow high-bar squat (Larsen 2021)
Controlled dip, strong drive up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Quarter Squat, video (movement reference only)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Larsen et al. 2021, stance width and bar placement in back squats: kinematics, kinetics and EMG (Front Sports Act Living)

cautions: Squat inside a rack with the safety arms set just below your bottom position, or with a spotter; the rack drawn here shows only the J-hooks.
Heavy quarter squats load the spine as much as the legs: build up gradually and use a belt only if you already brace well.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: shorten the range further or use a box to control depth.
Shoulder discomfort holding the bar: widen the grip a little.
regressions: Bodyweight squat to a high box.
progressions: Jump squat with a light bar.
